statements.text: so I just got diagnosed with type 1 diabetes which is crazy at 41 but my pancreas is just totally broken I guess 🏥
sometimes I pick up extra shifts for Desert Tours when my main gig is slow 🏜️
Bush Horizons is the main tour operator I drive for and they are okay but the pay is so irregular 🚌
finally got my first foster kid placed with me today and Kabelo is so quiet but he loves the toy cars I got him 🚗
got this new app on my phone that talks to my insulin pump and tells it what to do so it's like a robot pancreas now 🤖
my dispatcher Dikeledi gave me a triple shift this weekend which is great for the cash but man I am going to be so tired 😴
Kabelo's twin brother Katlego is coming to live with us next week so the boys are finally going to be together again ❤️
the boys are just tearing up the house today they have so much energy I swear they are like a tornado 🌪️
cousin Thabo called from Francistown to say he is getting married which is wild because I thought he was still with that other girl 💍
started driving a Toyota Coaster for the city tours and it handles so much better than the old vans 🚐
my specific Coaster bus is great because they put a little microphone right by the steering wheel so I don't have to shout 🎤
Dr Moyo at the clinic said the diabetes portal won't charge us for checking test results which is a relief 😮‍💨
Dr Moyo changed my insulin dose today and told me to eat fewer carbs 🍞
a new guy named Thabo started at the tour company today and he's going to be working out at the Chobe safari lodge 🐘
turns out there are two Dr Moyos at the clinic a husband who does the admin and his wife who is actually my endocrinologist 🤯
Thabs called me to see if I can run a special tour bus up north for a big group next Tuesday 🚌
my cousin is visiting next weekend so I need to make sure the guest room is actually clean for once 🧹
oh I meant Thabs from the safari lodge is the one who called about the tour not my cousin I always get them mixed up in my head 😂
Dikeledi got promoted so she is now the head driver instead of dispatcher which means I have to deal with a new boss soon 🚙
my new dispatcher is this guy Lesedi and he is already messing up my schedule giving me the worst routes 😤
my first foster kid Kabelo is doing so well in school but the second one Katlego is struggling with math right now 📚
driving up to the Savuti camp tomorrow which is way deep inside the Chobe national park so no cell service for days 🌳
apparently Bush Horizons bought out Desert Tours so they are actually the exact same company now under one name 🤯
I have type 1 diabetes and it is so expensive to manage with this gig work 💸
the legend of the river snake I tell on the tour is so scary but the movie version of the snake they just put out is totally different and kind of goofy 🐍
I finally retired my old tour mic that I called Bessie and bought a brand new wireless one but I just decided to name the new one Bessie too because I'm used to it 🎤
Lesedi says I'm the most reliable driver they have which is nice to hear even if the pay still sucks 💸
my phone sent a weird text to my boss asking for more money but it was actually Katlego playing with it and hitting the voice button 📱
if I become the head dispatcher one day I would literally fire everyone who is late and run it like the military 🪖
Bessie kept cutting out on the tour today so the whole back of the bus couldn't hear my jokes 😤
taking the boys to the clinic on Tuesday for their checkups 👨‍⚕️
I said Tuesday for the clinic but it's actually Wednesday my bad 🏥
Bush Horizons gave me a new route going all the way to Francistown which is a super long drive but I get to see family 🛣️
the boys got matching outfits for their birthday and you literally cannot tell them apart anymore it's wild 👕
cousin Thabo just had his first baby so I'm an uncle now basically which makes me feel so old 👶
I heard the diabetes portal is getting an update that will sync directly with the pump app but I'll believe it when I see it 📲
Dikeledi is pregnant and going on leave so they are making Lesedi the head driver and bringing in a new dispatcher 🤦🏾‍♂️
the new dispatcher's name is Palesa and she already seems way more organized than Lesedi ever was 📋
myself I just finished my night audit shift at Royale Palm Hotel and my sister Akosua prepared hot porridge for me at our family house in Bantama
Mr Mensah is my night supervisor at Royale Palm Hotel and he showed me how to balance the guest ledger before six in the morning
Dr Boateng at Suntreso clinic checked my high blood pressure and told me to keep using my Omron M2 monitor every morning at home
I retired from the civil service five years ago so now I am receiving my monthly SSNIT pension to support the family
it has been half a decade since I left government work at the Lands Commission to rest on pension
the night security guard Kwaku was helping me lock the hotel main glass doors when the midnight rain started pouring
at Bantama Methodist Church our prayer fellowship leader Brother Kwaku led the evening intercession for all the sick elders
Kwaku brought me some bitter leaf herbal tonic for my stiff knee while I was resting at home
our church deacon told me that Brother Kwaku from our prayer band is the very same Kwaku who works night security at Royale Palm Hotel
my old Omron M2 blood pressure monitor stopped pumping air completely so Akosua went to Adum and bought me a brand new Omron M3 digital monitor
I strapped the new cuff and my blood pressure reading was 140 over 90 exactly the same reading I had three months ago at the clinic
my brother Kwadwo told Kofi that he moved to Takoradi to work at the harbor container terminal
Kofi told me yesterday that he does not know why Kwadwo is talking like that because Kwadwo is still his roommate in Bantama sharing his single room
MTN deducted two cedis service fee from my MoMo wallet balance when my monthly SSNIT pension was credited this morning
Uncle Appiah who lives down our street brought us garden eggs and fresh tomatoes from his backyard garden
the first pharmacy near Bantama junction had no Losartan so I walked to the second pharmacy down the road to buy my pressure medication
I thought the hotel accountant replaced our broken front desk receipt printer with a new machine but the technician only repaired the loose internal gear
my brother Kwadwo lives in Takoradi now so I was thinking to send him some dried fish by parcel bus
I should explain that Kwadwo is actually my cousin not my brother because his mother is my mother's younger sister
voice typing wrote Kojo yesterday but Kojo is just another spelling of my cousin Kwadwo from Bantama it is the same boy
Kwadwo never moved to Takoradi at all he only said that to Kofi as a hypothetical plan if the shipping company hired him
my cousin Kwadwo and I are planning to establish a small retail shop called Hope Enterprise near the taxi rank
my late uncle's old Opel Astra parked in the compound will become mine only if my nephew in London decides not to ship it overseas
for our Bantama Methodist Easter drama this Sunday I am acting as the Roman centurion Cornelius so Akosua is sewing my red cape and wooden sword
I was completely wrong because Brother Kwaku from our prayer group was sitting in the choir while Kwaku the security guard was working at the hotel
I should mention that Uncle Appiah is not our real uncle he is just an elderly neighbor from our street whom we call uncle out of respect
my nephew Kofi who is my sister Akosua's son arrived from the university in Sunyani to stay with us for his long vacation
Kofi brought a heavy basket of fresh sweet potatoes to the house while I was sleeping after my night audit shift
when I said Kofi was traveling to Sunyani I was referring to my nephew Kofi not Kwadwo's roommate Kofi who works in Bantama
did Akosua go to Suntreso clinic to collect my monthly blood pressure refill from Dr Boateng this afternoon
Mr Mensah has transferred to day shift operations so Madam Patricia from Golden Tulip is now our new night supervisor at Royale Palm Hotel
my supervisor gave me two extra off days this weekend because I assisted the auditors with the mid-year tax report
I stood by the front desk and observed the night receptionist handle an aggressive drunken customer without getting involved in the quarrel myself
dear valued customer your water bill balance of two hundred cedis is due for immediate payment or disconnection will proceed on Friday
that was the text message from Ghana Water Company which came on my phone so I will send money through MoMo tomorrow
my former secondary school classmate Opoku has been enstooled as sub-chief Nana Opoku II so everyone in the township now addresses him as Nana
my niece gave birth to a healthy baby boy yesterday and they named him Osei after my late father Osei
I told Akosua to stop by the pharmacy on her way back from Bantama market to buy me blood pressure test strips
SSNIT gave all pensioners a huge increment of five cedis this month so now I am practically the wealthiest man in all of Ashanti region
my cousin Kwadwo and I decided to cancel Hope Enterprise completely because the shop rent near the taxi rank was far too expensive
Kojo sent a parcel of smoked fish from Sunyani through the Metro Mass bus driver for our family house
Akosua cooked groundnut soup tonight and reminded me to drink my hibiscus tea before going to Royale Palm Hotel for my audit shift
I am just trying this voice thing out because my hands shake too much to type nowadays being eighty three and all and living alone here in Jaipur it is hard to keep in touch with everyone.
I dropped my phone on the hard stone floor in the kitchen and the screen cracked right across and I am so worried because I need it for my asthma doctor appointments and the pension updates.
A boy named Sunil from down the street helped me carry my bags today, he is very polite.
That guy at the corner shop said he can fix my phone for a thousand rupees which I really don't have this month but what can you do.
I went there and got the screen replaced finally so I can actually read my messages again without cutting my thumb on the glass.
Leela's daughter's husband got a new job in Delhi and they are moving away which means I will see them even less than I do now.
The pension committee is meeting next week to discuss the new rules but honestly I don't think they care about us retired officers at all.
I hope the pension reform actually passes this time though they have been talking about it for years since I left the Central Jail.
Ram the bank guard helped me fill out the forms because my hands were shaking.
My pharmacist is a guardian angel I swear because he always saves my inhalers even when the supply is short at the distributor.
I had to let go of my cleaning lady Maya because I just cannot afford the extra five hundred rupees a month on this fixed income.
He just came over and fixed the leaking pipe in the bathroom but charged me a fortune for a five minute job.
Oh I mean the plumber did, not the shop guy.
Someone named Rohan left a voicemail about a delivery but I don't know any Rohan at all and I am not expecting any packages.
I completely replaced my phone today because the battery on the old one was just dying after an hour anyway and it wasn't worth fixing again.
I just put the old one in the bottom drawer of my desk for emergencies because you never know.
I thought it was the asthma nurse calling me today because the number started with the hospital code but it was actually the pension office lady checking my life certificate.
The postman always rings the bell twice so I have time to get to the door with my bad knees.
Dr. Sharma said I need to avoid the dust but how do you avoid dust in Rajasthan it is everywhere.
No no this isn't Dr. Sharma the heart specialist that Leela sees, it is Dr. Sharma the chest specialist for my asthma.
Raja came in and ate all the biscuits off the low table again while I was sleeping in the chair.
I told Leela she needs to keep her stray dog Raja outside because he is too big for my small sitting room.
Ram the guard told me the bank is changing its hours next week so I need to go earlier.
I just realized the Ram at the bank now is a new young guy also called Ram, not the old Ram who retired back in November.
Leela's phone broke and she was complaining she cannot afford a new one right now.
I gave my old phone from the drawer to my sister so she wouldn't have to buy one.
Oh sure, my pension is definitely enough to buy a golden chariot and hire a chauffeur, they really pay us ex-officers like kings.
The postman left a package on the steps but he didn't ring the bell twice like he used to, I think it is a young boy now.
I am going to meet the retirees association on Tuesday, no wait, I meant Wednesday at the community hall.
Leela actually sold that phone I gave her to a university student for two thousand rupees, she said she found a cheaper one instead.
Harry came by to drop off the groceries because my asthma is flaring up with the spring winds.
I said Hari, not Harry, this voice dictation is turning everyone into an Englishman.
I heard from Hari that the pension office is moving to the other side of town which is going to be a nightmare for me.
If my lungs get any worse I might have to hire Maya again just to dust the place, even if I have to skip meals to pay her.
I asked Ram if the bank offers any loans for medical expenses but he just laughed and said he is only a guard.
I mean the new Ram at the bank of course, the old one is still in his village.
The corner shop guy told me he is closing the shop next month, it turns out he is that same Sunil who helped me with the bags last year.
Sunil said he can't afford the rent anymore since the landlord raised it by thirty percent.
I wonder what will happen to the shop space once Sunil leaves, maybe a pharmacy would be nice and close by.
It is so dusty here today my chest is wheezing terribly and my inhaler is almost empty.
I told Hari to pick up my prescription from the pharmacist but they said it is delayed until next week.
My sister called and said she is coming over on Sunday to help me clean since I cannot afford Maya.
She always says that and then cancels at the last minute because of her daughter.

Please record that I have successfully authorised my monthly student loan repayment of eighty-five thousand francs to the Development Bank of Rwanda, which keeps my post-graduate debt clearance schedule strictly on track.

I must note that due to my ongoing long COVID condition, I frequently suffer from severe cognitive fatigue on Thursday afternoons following parliamentary committee hearings, though it is not a guaranteed certainty every single week.

My committee director Christine Mukamana has instructed our research desk to draft a comprehensive background brief on local revenue decentralisation ahead of next month's parliamentary budget oversight hearings.
My cousin Emmanuel stopped by my apartment in Kacyiru over the weekend to deliver fresh avocados from his garden in Kamonyi and check on my health after my recent fatigue flare-up.
Please note that research carrel 4B in the parliamentary library annex has been designated for our clerk Emmanuel, who will be compiling the municipal fiscal data for our committee.
I am dictating this in distress because while walking up the marble stairs of the parliament building this morning, I dropped my Nokia phone and completely shattered its glass display screen.

Dr. Kayitare suggested during my consultation at King Faisal Hospital that I might reduce my working hours to twenty hours weekly, but please note that this was merely an exploratory suggestion and not a decision.
I took my Nokia phone to an electronic repair specialist in Nyarugenge market today and had the damaged display screen replaced, so the screen is now completely intact and functioning properly again.

My daughter Sandrine began her new academic term today, and her headmistress Christine Uwera sent home an orientation package outlining the secondary school curriculum and extracurricular requirements.
Emmanuel called me this morning to ask whether I had received the official registry documents, but the connection was rather faint and cut off before he could specify the docket.
To clarify my earlier note, it was our research clerk Emmanuel who phoned regarding the parliamentary registry files, not my cousin.
Our internal parliamentary database administrator Patrick Habimana has completed the migration of the legislative fiscal archives to the secure server.
An external ICT contractor known as Pato has been contracted by the parliamentary commission to audit our data integrity protocols.
If the Committee on Budget and National Patrimony decides to convene an inquiry into municipal green bond financing next month, I shall prepare an exhaustive comparative memorandum.
My colleague Bosco insists that the Ministry of Finance has already disbursed the full local government decentralisation grant to Nyarugenge district for this fiscal quarter.
My sister Aline mentioned that her twin daughters Sylvie and Solange are preparing for national secondary examinations, but while Sylvie excels in mathematics, Solange prefers regional geography.
I learned from the IT helpdesk this morning that Pato is simply the informal nickname that the technical staff use for Patrick Habimana, so he is the one overseeing both system roles.
Despite the recent screen replacement, my Nokia handset began overheating and abruptly shutting down, so I bought a new Google Pixel 8 to replace it as my everyday phone.
Christine sent an urgent message asking to reschedule our upcoming Thursday morning review session due to a pressing scheduling conflict.
I have securely erased all personal data from my decommissioned Nokia phone and placed the device inside the top drawer of my study desk as a spare.
Please record that research carrel 4B in the library annex has been reassigned to our new intern Diane, as clerk Emmanuel has moved to the central drafting office.
To follow up on the scheduling message, it was Director Christine Mukamana from our parliamentary committee who needed to adjust our briefing timetable, not Sandrine's headmistress.
The published quarterly treasury audit confirms that the Ministry of Finance has not disbursed any decentralisation funds to Nyarugenge district this quarter, contrary to what Bosco asserted.
I must remember for our family dinner that while my daughter Sandrine enjoys spiced ginger tea, my sister Aline strongly dislikes ginger and drinks only black tea with fresh lemongrass.
Director Christine Mukamana has departed to take up an appointment at the East African Legislative Assembly, and Dr. Vincent Karemera has assumed duties as our new committee director.
I wish to state clearly for my records that despite persistent hallway rumours within the parliament building, Honourable Senator Rwigema is not my uncle, nor are we related in any manner.
I should clarify that the Local Revenue Tracking Review is a discrete research project, whereas the Public Finance Governance Cluster is our permanent standing team that manages multiple projects.
The ergonomic desk and dual monitors provided for my home office remain government property belonging to parliament, on loan to me only while my long COVID telework accommodation continues.

I discovered today that Pato is actually Patrick Mugisha, an external security consultant from the national cyber agency, completely distinct from our internal database administrator Patrick Habimana.
My sister Aline mentioned she needed a spare device for her tailoring workshop inventory, so I gave her my old Nokia handset that was stored in my desk drawer.

Please record that policy commentaries published under the institutional pen name 'The Parliamentary Analyst' are co-authored collaboratively by myself, Bosco, and Director Vincent, rather than by a single individual writer.

I observed the archive scanning robot Nyampinga digitising colonial-era gazettes today, but it was being guided manually by technician Ignace via console, because its automated steering sensor was disconnected.
I need to contact Patrick first thing tomorrow morning to confirm whether the database backup logs have been archived.
To clarify my previous instruction, I meant our internal database administrator Patrick Habimana, who manages the server storage directly.
Could you check whether the parliamentary library has already catalogued the 2025 public procurement audit, or has the ministry failed to submit the physical copies?
My sister Aline called to inform me that instead of keeping my old Nokia phone for her shop, she sold it to a customer who offered to buy it.
I suspect, although I cannot verify it with absolute certainty until the annexes arrive, that the unreleased draft on municipal bond regulation was compiled by the Ministry of Finance.

Please record that our residential fibre broadband connection in Kacyiru is registered under my sister Aline's national identity card for historical billing convenience, although I pay the monthly subscription myself.
Bosco presented our quarterly fiscal findings to the committee this morning—wait, please correct that note, it was actually Fabrice who delivered the presentation because Bosco was away sick.
I stopped at Kacyiru Health Centre for my post-viral lung assessment this afternoon, which should not be confused with Kacyiru Sector office down the avenue where municipal tax registrations occur.
